## Brackets on both sides {#both-sides}

Expand each side before gathering the unknown terms. A negative or fractional solution can be correct.

:::::: {.example-pair}
::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$4(2x-3)=3(x+6)$

::: {.fragment}

[Expand both brackets.]{.annotation}

$8x-12=3x+18$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Subtract $3x$ from both sides.]{.annotation}

$5x-12=18$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Add $12$ to both sides.]{.annotation}

$5x=30$

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Divide both sides by $5$.]{.annotation}

$\dfrac{5x}{5}=\dfrac{30}{5}\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=6$

:::
:::::
::::: {.paper}
::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$4(2x-3)=3(x-6)$

Only $+6$ changes to $-6$. Solve on paper and leave your answer as an exact fraction.

:::
::: {.fragment}

[Check your working]{.annotation}

$\begin{aligned}
8x-12&=3x-18\\
5x-12&=-18\\
5x&=-6\\
\dfrac{5x}{5}&=\dfrac{-6}{5}\\
x&=-\dfrac65
\end{aligned}$

The right-hand constant changes sign; the solving method stays the same.

:::
:::::
::::::
